title: Lamb Chop Curry
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb shoulder in a rich spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Lamb shoulder pieces browned and simmered in a deep spiced tomato sauce until the meat is very tender. Serve with rice or naan.
sourceNotes: Based on a North Indian masala-style braised lamb, adapted for lamb shoulder pieces cut bone-in.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce in portions. Reheat gently from thawed on the hob, adding a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double quantities work well in a large pot. Cook time stays the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The curry improves overnight as the sauce thickens and the spices settle. Reheat gently before serving.

content.text: This is a slow braise rather than a quick curry. The lamb needs time in the sauce to become tender all the way through. Brown the meat properly before adding liquid, as that colour builds the depth of flavour in the finished dish.

items.prepNote: cut into large pieces, bone-in if possible

content.text: Heat the oil in the large saucepan over a high heat. Brown the lamb pieces in batches on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce to a medium heat and add the onion. Cook for 12 minutes until deep golden. Stir regularly and scrape the base.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 2 minutes. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 1 minute more.
Add the tinned tomatoes and salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and the oil starts to show at the edges.
Return the lamb to the pan and add the water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook on a low heat for 60 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Remove the lid and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce. Stir in the garam masala and yoghurt over a low heat.
Rest for 10 minutes. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with rice or naan.

items.symptom: The meat is still tough after an hour.
items.cause: The simmer was too fierce, seizing the fibres rather than relaxing them.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low so the liquid barely moves. Add a little more water if needed and cook for another 20 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes sharp and acidic.
items.cause: The tinned tomatoes were not cooked long enough to lose their raw edge.
items.fix: Cook the tomatoes with the spices for a full 8 minutes before adding the lamb and water.

items.symptom: The yoghurt splits when stirred in.
items.cause: The heat was too high when the yoghurt was added.
items.fix: Take the pan off the heat, stir the yoghurt in, then return to the lowest setting for 2 minutes only.
